strings.addWord.intro: A text language's lists tell Unwrap lines which hyphen belongs to the word; a programming language's sets colour the word. The file is written into the folder of that kind, and the folder is reread at once.
strings.addWord.kind.name: Add to
strings.addWord.newName.desc: The name of the language; it becomes <Name>.json in the dictionary folder.
strings.addWord.newName.name: New dictionary name
strings.addWord.programming.desc: Only languages with word lists: the plugin's keyword tables and your own definitions. A language with a grammar has no list to add to.
strings.addWord.role.desc: Which set the word joins, and therefore its colour.
strings.addWord.role.name: Element
strings.addWord.text.desc: Its dictionary is created from the plugin's own lists when the folder has no file for it yet.
strings.addWord.title: Add to dictionary
strings.addWord.word.desc: As it is written. A hyphen at the end (кое-) makes it a prefix, one at the start (-нибудь) a particle.
strings.addWord.word.name: Word
strings.button.chooseFolder.tooltip: Pick the folder in the file explorer; the current one is created first and opened
strings.button.createExample.tooltip: Pick a language; its example file is written into the folder from the plugin's own definition
strings.button.reread.tooltip: Read the language, palette and dictionary folders again
strings.command.examplePalette: Create example palette for a language
strings.hotkey.add-cursor-above.meaning: a cursor on the line above, in the same column (at the end of a shorter line)
strings.hotkey.add-cursor-above.name: Add cursor above
strings.hotkey.add-cursor-below.meaning: a cursor on the line below
strings.hotkey.add-cursor-below.name: Add cursor below
strings.hotkey.completion.meaning: the words of this file and what the language knows
strings.hotkey.completion.name: Word completion
strings.hotkey.copy-line-down.name: Copy line down
strings.hotkey.copy-line-up.name: Copy line up
strings.hotkey.find-next-alt.name: Next match (second key)
strings.hotkey.find-next.meaning: next match, panel open or not
strings.hotkey.find-next.name: Next match
strings.hotkey.find-previous.name: Previous match
strings.hotkey.move-line-down.name: Move line down
strings.hotkey.move-line-up.meaning: move the line (or the selected lines) up
strings.hotkey.move-line-up.name: Move line up
strings.hotkey.rename.meaning: Obsidian's rename dialog for the file
strings.hotkey.rename.name: Rename file
strings.hotkey.replace-all.meaning: replace every match (panel open; in the Replace field, Enter replaces one)
strings.hotkey.replace-all.name: Replace all
strings.hotkey.replace.meaning: the same panel with the Replace row (editor only)
strings.hotkey.replace.name: Search and replace
strings.hotkey.search.meaning: open the search panel (Escape closes it)
strings.hotkey.search.name: Search
strings.hotkey.select-all-matches.meaning: every match becomes a selection and the text takes the focus: typing changes all of them (panel open)
strings.hotkey.select-all-matches.name: Select all matches
strings.hotkey.select-all-occurrences.meaning: every occurrence of the selected text (or of the word at the cursor), also after Add next occurrence
strings.hotkey.select-all-occurrences.name: Select all occurrences
strings.hotkey.select-line.name: Select line
strings.hotkey.select-next-occurrence.meaning: the next occurrence of the selected text becomes another selection
strings.hotkey.select-next-occurrence.name: Add next occurrence
strings.hotkey.toggle-block-comment.meaning: the language's block comment around the selection
strings.hotkey.toggle-block-comment.name: Toggle block comment
strings.hotkey.toggle-line-comment.meaning: the language's line comment on the selected lines
strings.hotkey.toggle-line-comment.name: Toggle line comment
strings.largeFile.body: This file is {size}, above the {limit} limit for opening in the editor. It is shown as a preview. Editing a file this size can be slow and use a lot of memory, especially on a phone.
strings.largeFile.limitNote: The limit is a per-device setting of Native File Editor.
strings.largeFile.title: Large file
strings.menu.case.title: Title Case
strings.newFile.name.placeholder: File name, e.g. notes or notes.ts
strings.newFile.title: New file
strings.newFile.type.desc: Type letters of the extension or language: tt finds txt, http, targets
strings.newFile.type.name: Extension or language
strings.newFile.warn.dotFile: .{extension} is a dot-file: Obsidian hides it, so it will not appear in the file explorer and Native File Editor cannot open it. The file is created all the same.
strings.newFile.warn.noExtension: Native File Editor does not open a file without an extension. The file is created all the same; Obsidian decides what opens it.
strings.newFile.warn.unknown: Native File Editor does not open .{extension} files. The file is created all the same; Obsidian decides what opens it.
strings.notice.comment.block.none: No block comment is known for {language}.
strings.notice.comment.line.none: No line comment is known for {language}.
strings.notice.create.failed: Native File Editor could not create {path}: {error}
strings.notice.device.reset: Native File Editor: device settings reset.
strings.notice.dictionaries.problems.one: Native File Editor: {count} dictionary not loaded; see the plugin log.
strings.notice.dictionaries.problems.other: Native File Editor: {count} dictionaries not loaded; see the plugin log.
strings.notice.dictionary.added: Native File Editor: {word} added to the {list} of {language} ({path})
strings.notice.dictionary.exampleFailed: Native File Editor: could not write the example dictionary: {error}
strings.notice.dictionary.noBundled: Native File Editor: {language} has no bundled dictionary; a file of that name in the folder makes one.
strings.notice.dictionary.notAWord: Native File Editor: that is not a word a dictionary can hold.
strings.notice.extension.invalid: Native File Editor: an extension is letters, digits, _ + or -.
strings.notice.folder.outsideVault: Native File Editor: the folder must be inside the vault.
strings.notice.highlight.failed: Native File Editor: highlighting failed for this file; shown as plain text. Details are in the plugin log.
strings.notice.keys.conflict: Native File Editor: {chord} is already used by {actions}. Both rows keep it; the first in the list wins. Change one of them.
strings.notice.keys.obsidian: Native File Editor: {chord} is Obsidian's {commands}, which runs first: inside the text it will not reach {action}. Saved anyway; change it here or under Obsidian's Hotkeys.
strings.notice.keyword.added: Native File Editor: {word} added to the {role} set of {language} ({path})
strings.notice.keyword.already: Native File Editor: {language} already had {word} as a {role}.
strings.notice.language.exampleFailed: Native File Editor: could not write the example definition: {error}
strings.notice.language.failed: Native File Editor: the {language} language failed to load; {file} opened as plain text.
strings.notice.language.noTable: Native File Editor: {language} is a grammar, not a keyword table; only keyword-based languages have an example definition.
strings.notice.language.noWordList: Native File Editor: {language} has no word list to add to (a grammar colours it), or the word has a space in it.
strings.notice.languages.problems.one: Native File Editor: {count} language definition not loaded; see the plugin log.
strings.notice.languages.problems.other: Native File Editor: {count} language definitions not loaded; see the plugin log.
strings.notice.locale.problem: Native File Editor: {file} was not loaded ({error}); the plugin stays in English.
strings.notice.palette.failed: Native File Editor: could not write the example palette: {error}
strings.notice.run.command.invalid: Native File Editor: the command line needs a program first, then its arguments.
strings.notice.run.steps.invalid: Native File Editor: each step needs a program first, then its arguments; steps are separated by &&.
strings.notice.save.failed: Native File Editor could not save {file}: {error}
strings.notice.unwrap.done: Unwrap lines: {breaks} removed at a wrap width of {width}{words}.
strings.notice.unwrap.none: Unwrap lines: no hard-wrapped lines found.
strings.notice.unwrap.notProse: Unwrap lines: this does not look like wrapped prose (width {width}); select the paragraphs to unwrap and try again.
strings.notice.unwrap.nothing: Unwrap lines: nothing to join at a wrap width of {width}.
strings.notice.word.failed: Native File Editor: could not add the word: {error}
strings.notice.wrap.done: Wrap lines: {lines} cut at {width} characters, {breaks} added.
strings.notice.wrap.none: Wrap lines: no line is longer than {width} characters.
strings.notice.yielded: Native File Editor left {parts}. Take them over per extension in its settings.
strings.readOnly.body: {file} is not valid UTF-8. It is shown decoded as {encoding}, which is a guess, so it opened read-only: writing a guess back could change bytes you never touched.
strings.readOnly.choices: Create UTF-8 copy writes {copy} beside it and opens the copy in the editor; the original is left alone. Edit as {encoding} edits the original and writes it back in that encoding; a character the encoding has no byte for stops the save until it is removed.
strings.readOnly.title: Read-only file
strings.run.copy.tooltip: Copy the view that is showing: the output, or the whole log
strings.run.error.desktopOnly: running a program needs the desktop app
strings.run.error.noTempDir: this runner needs a temp directory, which is not available here
strings.run.noRunner: No runner for this file; add one in settings
strings.run.resize: Drag to resize the output panel
strings.run.tab.log.tooltip: The console: the command, everything the program logged, a page's errors and refusals, the outcome
strings.run.tab.output.tooltip: The result: a page, or what the program wrote out
strings.search.selectAll.tooltip: every match becomes a cursor and the text takes the focus; what you type then changes all of them (Escape: one cursor)
strings.settings.dictionaries.example.placeholde: Text language for the example dictionary
strings.settings.dictionaries.folder.desc: One .json per text language (name, prefixes, suffixes, words). A file named after a bundled language adds to it, or replaces it with "replace": true; any other name is a language of its own. Create example writes the plugin's own lists; edit them, then Reread.
strings.settings.dictionaries.folder.name: Dictionary folder
strings.settings.dictionaries.heading: Dictionaries
strings.settings.dictionaries.toggle.desc: JSON word lists from the dictionary folder tell Unwrap lines which hyphen belongs to a word (кое-що, self-evident) and which one a printer left at a line end. Off: the plugin's own lists for fifteen languages apply.
strings.settings.dictionaries.toggle.name: Use custom dictionaries
strings.settings.editor.dateFormat.desc: What Insert ▸ Date in the text's context menu writes, in the moment.js syntax Obsidian's Templates plugin uses (YYYY, MM, DD, dddd, MMMM …). Empty: the Templates plugin's own format if it has one, else YYYY-MM-DD.
strings.settings.editor.dateFormat.name: Date format
strings.settings.editor.direction.desc: Auto reads each line by its first letter (an Arabic or Hebrew line runs right to left, the rest left to right); the two others force the whole document. Also in the pane's menu.
strings.settings.editor.direction.name: Text direction
strings.settings.editor.heading: Editor
strings.settings.editor.invisibles.desc: Spaces as dots, tabs as arrows and a line-ending badge at the end of every line. Also in the pane's header and its menu.
strings.settings.editor.invisibles.name: Show invisibles
strings.settings.editor.lineNumbers.name: Line numbers
strings.settings.editor.searchHints.desc: "Next (F3)", "Previous (Shift+F3)" and so on in the search panel. Off shows the plain words; the tooltips keep the shortcuts.
strings.settings.editor.searchHints.name: Shortcut hints on search buttons
strings.settings.editor.tabSize.name: Tab size
strings.settings.editor.tabSpaces.name: Tab inserts spaces
strings.settings.editor.timeFormat.desc: The time part of Insert ▸ Date and time (HH:mm:ss, HH:mm, h:mm A …). Empty: the Templates plugin's own format if it has one, else HH:mm:ss.
strings.settings.editor.timeFormat.name: Time format
strings.settings.editor.wordWrap.name: Word wrap
strings.settings.fileTypes.custom.desc: Opens as {language}. Applied at once and at every start.
strings.settings.fileTypes.custom.heading: Custom file types
strings.settings.fileTypes.custom.none: None. Add an extension and pick the language that opens it; useful when you have written a language definition for it.
strings.settings.fileTypes.custom.prompt.desc: The extension without the dot, e.g. xl
strings.settings.fileTypes.custom.prompt.title: Custom file type
strings.settings.fileTypes.desc: Which extensions this plugin opens, and your own additions.
strings.settings.fileTypes.ext.desc: Takes effect after the plugin reloads.
strings.settings.fileTypes.ext.ownedBy: Currently opened by {owner}. Turn on to take it over. Takes effect after the plugin reloads.
strings.settings.fileTypes.heading: File types
strings.settings.fileTypes.known.heading: Known extensions
strings.settings.keys.change.tooltip: Change: press the new key combination (Escape cancels)
strings.settings.keys.editorNote: . Inside the text: a key Obsidian uses for its own hotkey does not reach it.
strings.settings.keys.guide.desc: Every key the editor answers to, and what the .* switch in the search panel understands, with the searches people reach for. The same guide is behind the ? in the pane's head bar.
strings.settings.keys.guide.name: Keys and regular expressions
strings.settings.keys.heading: Keys
strings.settings.keys.hotkeys.desc: Every key this plugin takes, and your changes to them. Defaults and changes are per platform (Windows and Linux, macOS), so a remap here does not land on another kind of machine. The guide behind the ? in the pane's head bar shows the same keys.
strings.settings.keys.hotkeys.name: Hotkeys
strings.settings.keys.howto.desc: The pencil records the next key combination you press for that row (Escape cancels); the arrow puts the default back. A change applies to panes opened afterwards. Keys that act inside the text (cursors, lines, block comment) cannot take a combination Obsidian keeps for itself; such a row shows the holder in the warning colour.
strings.settings.keys.howto.name: How to change one
strings.settings.keys.obsidian.editor: Obsidian's {commands} takes this key first: inside the text it does not arrive
strings.settings.keys.obsidian.scope: also Obsidian's {commands}: this pane takes it first while the text has the focus
strings.settings.keys.taken: already used by {actions} — the first of the two in this list wins
strings.settings.language.desc: The plugin speaks English unless a localization.json in its own folder says otherwise.
strings.settings.language.heading: Language
strings.settings.language.inForce: {language}, {translated} of {total} strings translated. Anything the file leaves out stays English. Edit the file and press Reread.
strings.settings.language.name: Localization
strings.settings.language.none: The plugin is in English. Put a localization.json into {file} and press Reread; the repository has an English copy to translate and a Ukrainian one.
strings.settings.language.openFolder.tooltip: Show the plugin's folder, where localization.json goes
strings.settings.languages.example.placeholder: Language for the example definition (keyword-based languages only)
strings.settings.languages.folder.desc: One .json per language. Create example writes the plugin's own table for a keyword-based language; edit it, then Reread.
strings.settings.languages.folder.name: Language folder
strings.settings.languages.heading: Languages
strings.settings.languages.toggle.desc: JSON definitions from the language folder (name, extensions, comment syntax, keyword sets) highlight files, replacing the plugin's own definition for the same extensions while the file is there.
strings.settings.languages.toggle.name: Use custom languages
strings.settings.opening.heading: Opening
strings.settings.opening.initialMode.desc: Preview renders instantly; the editor is built when you ask for it. Remember keeps the last mode per file on this device.
strings.settings.opening.initialMode.name: Initial mode
strings.settings.opening.largeFile.desc: Files above this size open in preview only, with a button to edit anyway. Per device.
strings.settings.opening.largeFile.name: Large file limit (MB)
strings.settings.palettes.example.placeholder: Language for the example palette (light and dark files)
strings.settings.palettes.folder.desc: Files are <Language>_light.css / <Language>_dark.css (or .xml from Notepad++, .js from a CodeMirror theme); a name that is no language applies to every file. A file in the folder is used while it is there; otherwise the plugin's own colours.
strings.settings.palettes.folder.name: Palette folder
strings.settings.palettes.heading: Palettes
strings.settings.palettes.toggle.desc: Colour files from the palette folder override the theme's colours for the files they name. Off: the editor follows the Obsidian theme.
strings.settings.palettes.toggle.name: Use custom palettes
strings.settings.plugin.heading: Plugin
strings.settings.plugin.reload.desc: Disable and enable Native File Editor: applies file-type changes and rereads everything. The settings window closes and reopens here.
strings.settings.plugin.reload.name: Reload plugin
strings.settings.plugin.reset.confirm.desc: Native File Editor forgets what it keeps for this device: {interpreters}, the Run switch, the timeout and output limit, the large-file limit and the remembered panel heights and modes. Shared settings in data.json are not touched. There is no undo.
strings.settings.plugin.reset.confirm.title: Reset this device's settings?
strings.settings.plugin.reset.desc: Forgets what is stored for this device in Obsidian's local storage, which a reinstall does not touch: the interpreters, the Run switch and limits, the large-file limit, remembered modes. Shared settings in data.json stay. Asks first.
strings.settings.plugin.reset.name: Reset this device's settings
strings.settings.run.enable.desc: Adds a Run button to the head bar and the commands Run file and Stop run. JavaScript runs in a sandbox inside Obsidian and web pages render inside Obsidian; any other language runs through an interpreter you add on the Interpreters page, on this device, with your permissions, only when you press Run. Off by default; nothing ever runs on its own.
strings.settings.run.enable.name: Enable Run
strings.settings.run.heading: Run (this device)
strings.settings.run.interpreter.command.tooltip: Edit the command line: the program, then its arguments; {file} is the file's path
strings.settings.run.interpreter.program.tooltip: Choose the program (for a compile-then-run language: the compiler, the first step)
strings.settings.run.interpreter.remove.tooltip: Remove this interpreter; the language goes back to what the plugin does by itself, if anything
strings.settings.run.interpreters.add.desc: One per language: pick the language, then the program that runs its files. The program replaces what the plugin does by itself for that language (the JavaScript sandbox, the page view). Languages that already have an interpreter are not offered.
strings.settings.run.interpreters.add.name: Add interpreter…
strings.settings.run.interpreters.desc: Programs that run your files on this device. Add a language, choose its program, or edit an existing command line.
strings.settings.run.interpreters.name: Interpreters (this device)
strings.settings.run.outputCap.desc: Output beyond this is dropped and the program is killed.
strings.settings.run.outputCap.name: Output limit (KB)
strings.settings.run.timeout.desc: A run longer than this is killed, with its child processes.
strings.settings.run.timeout.name: Timeout (seconds)
strings.view.badge.decodedByGuess: read-only: not valid UTF-8, shown as a guess
strings.view.badge.notSaved: not saved: "{char}" on line {line} has no byte in {encoding}
strings.view.badge.problemChar: Click to go to the character. Remove it, or create a UTF-8 copy from the menu.
strings.wrap.breakWords.desc: On, a word longer than the room left is cut at the width. Off, it stands on a line of its own, longer than the width.
strings.wrap.breakWords.name: Break long words
strings.wrap.intro: Every line longer than the width is cut into lines of at most that many characters, at spaces. Lines that already fit, blank lines, headings, lists, quotes, tables and code are left as they are.
strings.wrap.title: Wrap lines
strings.wrap.width.name: Line width
